title: Deeper/broader LibreCAD fork and LibreCAD_3 consumer reconciliation
scope: Read-only source/documentation comparison of the adjacent LibreCAD in-tree libdxfrw fork's generated coverage/roadmap documents, current LibreCAD_3 DWG policy/build integration, and the local compile-only compatibility guard. No sibling C++ function-by-function diff or build was performed. Refine integration readiness without counting correlated code as independent format evidence.

sources.name: Adjacent LibreCAD checkout
sources.evidence: The in-tree fork documents DWG read/write surfaces and has a versioned active roadmap plus a generated source inventory distinguishing dispatch/raw classifications from fixture-backed validation. The active roadmap keeps AC1032 evidence separate from inheritance alone.
sources.limit: Same libdxfrw implementation lineage, not an independent parser/writer or semantic vote. The sibling working tree has unrelated dirty files; the cited documents themselves were unchanged. No sibling build or application run was performed.

sources.name: LibreCAD_3 CMake build definition
sources.evidence: WITH_PERSISTENCE enables the vendored libdxfrw build; WITH_DWG_IMPORT is a separate OFF-by-default option. The build disables documentation/CLI/development-file installation and applies -Wno-error to dxfrw on non-MSVC compilers.
sources.limit: Mutable master source review only; no commit-bound checkout or build was used in this research pass. The warning policy makes the downstream build an integration check, not a replacement for strict upstream -Werror.

sources.name: LibreCAD_3 DWG product policy
sources.evidence: The application documents optional experimental DWG reading through dwgRW and no DWG writing.
sources.limit: Consumer policy, not a library capability or independent implementation result.

sources.name: Local LibreCAD_3 compatibility guard
sources.evidence: The target is an object-library compile check mirroring callback overrides and selected public fields/signatures; it does not link or run LibreCAD_3 or parse a drawing.
sources.limit: Useful fast API/layout compatibility signal only; not full adapter integration, file import, display, save, or semantic acceptance.

findings: LibreCAD's bundled fork is a related implementation snapshot and migration target. Its roadmap and source inventories can expand feature discovery, but static registration/counts and same-lineage behavior cannot independently establish correctness or support.
LibreCAD and LibreCAD_3 represent distinct downstream profiles: the former tracks in-tree DWG read/write development; the latter keeps DWG import opt-in/read-only and does not expose DWG writing.
The local lc3_compat_check target is narrower than an actual consumer source/build integration and must be described as compile-only API/layout evidence.
LibreCAD_3's non-MSVC -Wno-error integration policy does not satisfy the standalone library's strict -Werror requirement.
implementationReadyChecks: Reconcile selected sibling-fork deltas by exact source revision, format version, direction, adapter, owner/reference closure, and validation evidence before porting; require ODA-backed local behavior checks for wire-level changes.
Keep focused affected-target tests and lc3_compat_check as the cheap per-slice gates; do not add third-party DWG/DXF fixtures.

At one existing coarse compatibility checkpoint after shared API/adapter work, compile pinned LibreCAD and LibreCAD_3 adapter/persistence sources against the intended standalone branch and record exact revisions/toolchain/options.
Keep LibreCAD_3 default persistence (DWG import off) separate from its optional DWG-read profile; neither is a DWG-write or 3D-semantic pass.
If consumer sources/toolchains are unavailable, record NOT_RUN and self-unblock to the next ready local implementation item without waiting for an external fixture or platform.
